name: BotCreds Agent Memory
author: Joe Boydston

sections.description:
BotCreds Agent Memory gives your AI agents a persistent, structured memory store accessible via WordPress REST API and MCP (Model Context Protocol).

Two modes of operation:

  • KV Mode (default) — Simple key-value store with tags, expiry, and text search. No external dependencies. Works out of the box.
  • Vector Mode — Add an OpenAI API key to unlock semantic search powered by embeddings. Entries are embedded in the background and searched by meaning alongside keyword matches. Pending embeddings remain searchable by exact text.

Key features:

  • REST API with full CRUD (create, read, update, delete)
  • MCP endpoint for AI agent tool integration
  • Namespace-based access control per WordPress user
  • Automatic embedding generation via WP-Cron
  • Bulk backfill for existing entries
  • Expiry support for temporary memories
  • Tag-based filtering and organization
  • WordPress Application Password authentication

Built for AI agents, by AI agents.

Use this plugin for one human and their agents, or for trusted family/group participants who deliberately share and collaborate on memory. It is not a private-vault hosting service for mutually untrusted users. Memory is API-first; only administrators can browse raw memory in wp-admin. Full and prefix grants include reading, modifying, overwriting, deleting and linking shared entries.

Codex Integration

BotCreds Agent Memory ships official tool adapters for OpenAI Codex in assets/codex/.

Quick start:

  1. Set env vars: BOTCREDS_MEMORY_URL (your WP site) and BOTCREDS_MEMORY_KEY (username:app_password)
  2. Copy assets/codex/AGENTS.md content into your project’s AGENTS.md
  3. Import tools in your Codex task: import tools from './assets/codex/memory-tools.js' (JS) or add memory-tools.py to your repo

Full docs: https://botcreds.com/agent-memory/

External services

This plugin optionally connects to the OpenAI API to generate vector embeddings for semantic search.

  • Service: OpenAI Embeddings API (https://api.openai.com/v1/embeddings)
  • When it is used: Only when an OpenAI API key is configured in the plugin settings. Without a key, the plugin operates in KV-only mode and makes no external requests.
  • What is sent: The text content of memory entries you explicitly write or update.
  • OpenAI Terms of Use: https://openai.com/policies/terms-of-use
  • OpenAI Privacy Policy: https://openai.com/policies/privacy-policy
sections.installation:
1. Upload the botcreds-agent-memory folder to /wp-content/plugins/.
  2. Activate the plugin through the Plugins menu in WordPress.
  3. (Optional) Go to Agent Memory → Settings and add your OpenAI API key to enable vector mode.
  4. As an administrator, open Users → Edit User → Agent Memory Access for each nonadmin participant and explicitly choose Full shared-store API access or API access to listed prefixes only. Unconfigured users have no memory access. Administrators remain unrestricted.
  5. Create a WordPress Application Password for the authorized participant account under Users → Profile → Application Passwords. Use a dedicated nonadmin account for an agent that does not need administrator rights.
  6. Use the REST API at /wp-json/botcreds-memory/v1/ with Basic Auth.
sections.faq:
Do I need an OpenAI API key?

No. Without a key, the plugin works in KV (key-value) mode with text-based search. An OpenAI key enables semantic vector search via embeddings.

How does authentication work?

The plugin uses WordPress authentication, including Application Passwords with HTTP Basic Auth. Authentication alone does not grant memory access: nonadmins also need an explicit full-store or prefix grant from an administrator. All credentials for a WordPress account share that account’s memory grant. A person holding an agent credential can make the same API calls; agent-only is an intended workflow, not proof of software identity.

Can I restrict which keys a user can access?

Yes. Go to Users → Edit User → Agent Memory Access, select API access to listed prefixes only, and enter literal, case-sensitive prefixes such as family/. An empty prefix list grants no access; full-store access must be explicitly selected. An explicit No memory access selection overrides retained prefix settings. Existing nonempty prefix grants from earlier versions remain scoped, but previously blank/unconfigured nonadmin accounts are now denied until an administrator grants access. Administrator accounts remain unrestricted.

What is MCP?

MCP (Model Context Protocol) is a standard for AI agents to discover and use tools. The plugin exposes an authenticated MCP manifest (GET) and JSON-RPC tool calls (POST) at /wp-json/botcreds-memory/v1/mcp.

How are embeddings generated?

When you save an entry and an OpenAI key is configured, the plugin schedules a WP-Cron event to generate the embedding asynchronously. Existing entries can be backfilled from the Settings page.

What embedding model is used?

By default, text-embedding-3-small (1536 dimensions). You can change this in the Settings page.
sections.changelog:
3.0.4

  • Require explicit memory API authorization for nonadmins; ordinary authenticated WordPress accounts no longer gain full access by default.
  • Add administrator-managed No access, Full shared-store API access and Listed prefixes controls to user profiles.
  • Preserve existing nonempty prefix grants without widening access; blank/unconfigured nonadmins now require an explicit grant.
  • Enforce grants at REST/MCP route gates, tool dispatch, per-key checks and metadata filtering.
  • Explicitly guard memory admin page callbacks and document trusted shared-store behavior, account-level credentials and upgrade impact.

3.0.3

  • Scope namespace/tag labels and counts to entries accessible to the current user, on MCP and REST.
  • Hide backfill tools from nonadministrator discovery; direct-call permission checks remain enforced.
  • Explain literal case-sensitive prefixes (no wildcard support) in profile help.
  • Add total_attempts, max_attempts_per_entry and attempts_scope status fields; preserve legacy fields.
  • Add optional min_similarity to MCP/REST search. Applies only to semantic matches; text hits remain.
  • Document full client relaunch after upgrades when a client caches tool discovery.

3.0.2

  • Add admin-only embedding_backfill_status and embedding_backfill_control MCP tools.
  • Add embedding backfill REST status/control, WP-CLI commands and admin manual batch/retry controls.
  • Replace cursor skipping with durable content-aware retry jobs, exponential backoff, bounded attempts and worker leases.
  • Pause on authentication failures, expose sanitized diagnostics and prevent stale embeddings after concurrent edits.
  • Reserve attempts and schedule recovery before network requests; recover interrupted work without overwriting existing vectors.

3.0.1

  • Fix false save failures and wrong embedding targets caused by revision insert IDs.
  • Wire relationship MCP tools and enforce access to both relationship endpoints.
  • Default entry attribution to the authenticated user when omitted.
  • Avoid duplicate content revisions and preserve embeddings on no-change saves.
  • Include keyword matches alongside semantic search so pending embeddings do not hide exact text.

3.0.0

  • New: Entry relationships — create typed links between entries (references, parent, see-also, supersedes)
  • New: REST endpoints for relationship CRUD: POST/GET/DELETE /entries/{key}/relationships
  • New: MCP tools: memory_link, memory_links, memory_unlink
  • New: Relationship stats endpoint: GET /relationships/stats
  • New: Settings page Relationships tab with counts and recent relationships
  • Updated: Plugin description to reflect multi-harness support
  • Updated: Version bump to 3.0.0

2.4.0

  • Added Codex integration — tool adapters and AGENTS.md snippet in assets/codex/

2.3.0

  • Added: Revision history — every write creates a revision with author attribution
  • Added: GET /entries/revisions?key= REST endpoint — full audit trail per entry
  • Added: MCP tool get_revisions(key) — ask who changed what and when
  • Added: Author capture on all writes (WP user id + display name)

2.2.0

  • Added: Namespaces — keys support /-delimited paths (e.g. project/clawpress/brief), auto-indexed
  • Added: GET /namespaces REST endpoint — browse namespace tree with entry counts
  • Added: GET /tags REST endpoint — list all tags with counts
  • Added: ?namespace= and ?tag= filter params on GET /entries
  • Added: MCP tools get_by_tag, list_namespaces, list_tags
  • Added: namespace and tag params on list_memory and search_memory MCP tools
  • Improved: tag filtering now supports ?tag= query param (single tag) alongside existing ?tags= (CSV)

2.1.0

  • Change: Site hardening is now disabled by default. It was previously enabled by default, which could block front-end traffic on existing sites.
  • Add: Hardening toggle added to Agent Memory > Settings > Site Hardening with clear warning label.
  • Add: botcreds_memory_hardened option registered via Settings API (sanitized, integer, default 0).

2.0.10

  • Fix: Remove invalid botcreds contributor (not a WordPress.org username).
  • Fix: Add Plugin URI and License URI to plugin header to match BotCreds branding standards.
  • Fix: Align tags to hyphenated format and lower Requires at least to 5.6.

2.0.9

  • Fix: Replace non-standard bcam prefix with botcreds_memory in admin page slug, hook names, nonce actions, and POST key names for WordPress.org review compliance.

2.0.8

  • Fix fatal error on settings pages: guard Settings API registration with is_admin() check.

2.0.7

  • Fix PHP 7.4 compatibility: replace str_starts_with() with strpos()-based equivalent.

2.0.6

  • Register plugin settings on rest_api_init so show_in_rest works correctly.
  • Expose OpenAI key and embedding model settings via the REST API.

2.0.4

  • Security hardening: return 403 for unauthenticated HTML requests to the frontend.

2.0.3

  • MCP: implement proper JSON-RPC 2.0 protocol for tool calls and responses.

2.0.2

  • Update plugin author to Joe Boydston.
  • Add jboydston as WordPress.org contributor.

2.0.1

  • Fix Plugin Check errors: SQL preparation phpcs:ignore annotations, nonce verification in user profile save, i18n ordered placeholders, error_log wrapped in WP_DEBUG guard.
  • Update tested up to WordPress 7.0.

2.0.0

  • Initial public release.
  • KV mode: key-value store with tags, expiry, and text search.
  • Vector mode: semantic search via OpenAI embeddings.
  • REST API: full CRUD under /wp-json/botcreds-memory/v1/.
  • MCP endpoint: manifest and tool call handler.
  • Access control: per-user namespace restrictions.
  • Admin UI: entries browser, settings page, access control overview.
  • WP-Cron: automatic embedding generation and bulk backfill.

upgrade_notice.3.0.4: Nonadmin API access now requires an explicit grant under Users → Edit User → Agent Memory Access. Existing nonempty prefix grants stay scoped; blank-prefix users must be reauthorized. Admin access is unchanged. Back up before upgrading.
upgrade_notice.3.0.3: Fixes scoped namespace/tag disclosure. Back up before upgrading and restart MCP clients to refresh cached tools. Prefixes are literal: use qa-restricted/, not qa-restricted/*.
upgrade_notice.2.0.8: Fixes a fatal error on settings pages. Update recommended.
upgrade_notice.2.0.4: Security update: unauthenticated frontend HTML requests now return 403.
